drivingQuestion: Does water in an individual's cistern follow its owner if springs follow everyone?
outcomeNote: Resolved as collected water, supported by Shmuel.

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ רָמֵי לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב נַחְמָן, תְּנַן: בּוֹר שֶׁל יָחִיד — כְּרַגְלֵי הַיָּחִיד, וּרְמִינְהוּ: נְהָרוֹת הַמּוֹשְׁכִין וּמַעֲיָנוֹת הַנּוֹבְעִין — הֲרֵי הֵן כְּרַגְלֵי כׇּל אָדָם! אָמַר (רָבָא): הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן — בִּמְכוּנָּסִין. וְאִתְּמַר נָמֵי, אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: בִּמְכוּנָּסִין.
segments.en: «GEMARA:» «Rava raised a contradiction to Rav Naḥman: We learned» in the mishna that the water of «a cistern of an individual is as the feet of the individual; and» Rava «raised a contradiction» from the Tosefta (Beitza 4:8): Water drawn from «flowing rivers and flowing springs are as the feet of all people. Rava said: With what are we dealing here» in the mishna? «With» cisterns that contain «collected» water, not flowing water. «And it was also said» that «Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Avin said» that «Shmuel said:» The mishna applies only «to collected» water.
